title: Early metabolic defects in dexamethasone-exposed and undernourished intrauterine growth restricted rats.
ehr_evidence: Female and male (275–325 g) Sprague-Dawley OFA rats (Charles River Laboratories, France) were used for breeding and housed under specific pathogen-free conditions in an environmentally-controlled clean room at the School of Medicine animal facilities (Medical Center University, University of Geneva).
summary: Experimental study modeling intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) in rat pups via prenatal dexamethasone exposure or maternal undernutrition to assess early metabolic, pancreatic, and adipose tissue defects before weaning.
key_findings: DEX and UN pups had ~13% and 17% lower birth weight than controls (p<0.0001).
Hepatic Pck1 and G6pc mRNA increased by 46±19% and 101±35% in DEX pups, and 53±7% and 85±20% in UN pups at PND7 (p<0.05).
Basal glycaemia at PND21 was elevated in DEX (6.9±0.1 mmol/l) and UN (6.8±0.1 mmol/l) pups vs controls (6.2±0.2 mmol/l) (p<0.02).
GTT AUC was increased in DEX (868±27) and UN (870±26) pups vs controls (693±16 mmol/L*min) (p<0.0001).
Pancreatic islet number was reduced in DEX (62±5) and UN (52±4) pups vs controls (82±4 islets/section) (p<0.01).
Mean islet size was reduced in DEX (1462±66) and UN (1612±79) pups vs controls (1917±80 μm²) (p<0.02).
UN pups exhibited decreased glucose-induced insulin secretion at 15 min (0.51±0.09 vs 0.89±0.11 ng/mL, p<0.02).
DEX pups showed attenuated glycaemia drop in insulin tolerance test, indicating reduced insulin sensitivity.
UN pups had reduced epididymal white adipose tissue mass at PND21 (44±5 mg vs 71±7 mg controls, p<0.01).
captured_features: hepatic Pck1 and G6pc mRNA and protein levels
circulating corticosterone, leptin, insulin, and C-peptide levels
adipose tissue mass and gene expression
population: Sprague-Dawley rat pups (PND0-PND28) and gestating dams
exposure_domain: prenatal dexamethasone exposure, maternal undernutrition (caloric restriction)
limitations: study restricted to pre-weaning period without catch-up growth
physiological tests performed only on male pups to avoid sex confounding
insulin tolerance test less sensitive than euglycaemic hyperinsulinemic clamps
rat model limitations for direct human translation
